messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER: P1 - Serving runtime errors (us-west-2). Multiple container restarts observed during prefill path (GPU OOM / CUDA errors). Triggered 1930007777
Priya (oncall): I'm on it. Symptoms? which nodes/pods?
Ben (eng-runtime): Seeing repeated `CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY` then `CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS` in runtime logs. Containers restart, kube reports `OOMKilled` on the model-server prefill container. Example from pod runtime-abb2:
```
[2026-03-14T12:02:41Z] ERROR runtime: prefill failed: CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY
attempted allocation: 1.2GiB, available: 800MiB
stack: ...
```
Ben (eng-runtime): Prefill allocation grows linearly with prompt length because KV cache build isn't truncated. We have a few requests with huge context (40k-80k tokens) hitting the hosted API and triggering batching; the combined alloc exceeds GPU memory.
Alex (sre): Node telemetry: node-3 kernel messages show driver restart then kubelet restart. node-3 flapped 3x in last 12m. node-4 had one restart, both in us-west-2a.
Lina (Customer Success): Two customers reported 500s for chat completions ~12:02–12:15. One enterprise customer with SLA impact, they saw retries and degraded latency. CS is preparing an update.
Samir (eng-ml): We also see cuBLAS workspace allocations spiking. Mixed-precision fallback may be expanding memory use during prefill.
Priya (oncall): Immediate mitigation ideas: 1) fast-fail very long prefill requests at the router (reject > X tokens), 2) reduce batch concurrency for model on affected nodes, 3) cordon/drain flapping nodes, 4) add temporary routing to smaller-model fallback for heavy routes. Which can we do now?
Ben (eng-runtime): I'll push a hotfix to enforce `prefill_max_tokens=32768` at the router/ingress level and return a clear 413 with guidance. Can deploy canary to us-west-2.
deploy-bot: Deploy started: runtime-hotfix/prefill-limit -> canary (us-west-2)
Ben (eng-runtime): Canary logs show rejections are working: response payload:
```
HTTP/1.1 413 Payload Too Large
{ "error": "prefill tokens > 32768; shorten context or contact enterprise support for dedicated capacity" }
```
Priya (oncall): Alex, can you cordon node-3? It's flapping and causing host-level driver restarts.
Alex (sre): Cordon node-3 now, starting `kubectl drain node-3 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` to move pods. Drain in progress.
Ben (eng-runtime): After canary, restart rate dropped by ~70% on canary nodes. Non-canary still experiencing OOMs until traffic shifts. I'll add an emergency routing rule to divert heavy prefill routes to canary + fallback model.
Samir (eng-ml): Quick note: fallback model should be quantized but with smaller KV usage; recommend model-small-v2 for overflow. I'll add to route config.
Lina (Customer Success): Notifying impacted customers: sending status + workaround (shorten prompt, avoid full chat history). Escalating to enterprise TAMs.
Priya (oncall): Preliminary impact summary: two customers had >5% error rate over 15m window, multiple requests got 500 or connection resets, degraded latency for others. Marking incident as P1.
Ben (eng-runtime): One edge case: a massive prefill still caused host-level driver crash before admission could reject (likely raced allocation). For that host, we're isolating logs and will powercycle node-3 once drain completes to stabilize driver.
Alex (sre): node-3 drained, cordoned, and now powered cycle scheduled with infra. node-4 remains under observation but stabilized after traffic shift.
Priya (oncall): Next steps for 6h window: 1) keep prefill admission control in place, 2) monitor canary then roll to cluster, 3) add route-level `prefill_token_size` metric, 4) create synthetic test (80k token prefill) in CI to prevent regressions, 5) customer follow-ups and postmortem.
Samir (eng-ml): I'll add the synthetic test and a perf baseline for mixed-precision prefill behavior. Ben, can you add a short-circuit kill to the container if prefill allocation > safe threshold to avoid host driver instability?
Ben (eng-runtime): Yes, implementing a hard-kill earlier in the allocation path to fail the request rather than letting driver crash. Will include logs to surface token size and route id in error.
Priya (oncall): Handoff: Ben will take night on-call starting at 1930007800. Ben, you're owner for monitoring and executing rollback if restarts resume. Lina will continue customer comms. Document everything in the incident PM.
Ben (eng-runtime): Ack. I'll watch canary and node health, set alert if restart rate > 2/hr or error rate > 1%.
incident-bot: Incident P1 acknowledged and assigned to Ben (oncall). Ticket created: INC-1930007.
Priya (oncall): Thanks team — keep notes here. We'll stitch together logs/traces for the postmortem.
